bounded_slice.candidate: Observation identity authenticity escalation for the p1-sa-600 two-layer content/observation commitment model.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Local deterministic symbolic replay only. Compared producer-chosen nonce/UUID, repository immutable-object identity, and authenticated/signed provenance as abstract CanonicalInstanceID/ProvenanceCommitment mechanisms. model.authenticity_question: Which identity fields, if any, upgrade replay from byte-uniqueness to evidence that a distinct authenticated producer or repository event generated the observation?

mechanism_tests.reason: A producer can mint arbitrarily many fresh values. The field makes encodings distinct but provides no trust anchor, no Sybil resistance and no proof that distinct real observations occurred.

mechanism_tests.byte_uniqueness: pass for distinct immutable objects; identical content-addressed blobs may intentionally collapse
mechanism_tests.repository_event_identity: conditional pass when the exact immutable repository object is the event being claimed and is replay-retrievable
mechanism_tests.reason: A content-addressed blob or immutable commit/object identifier can bind replay to exact repository bytes/object history, but it does not by itself prove who produced them or that two repository objects correspond to independent real-world observations. Repository write authority/ref integrity remains a trust surface.

mechanism_tests.byte_uniqueness: pass when canonical signed tuple includes the instance identity
mechanism_tests.repository_event_identity: pass only for the exact signed/referenced object under the chosen protocol
mechanism_tests.producer_authenticity: conditional pass for possession of the signing/authentication credential
mechanism_tests.reason: A valid signature/authenticated assertion can bind canonical bytes to a credential, but key-to-producer identity, issuance, rotation/revocation, compromise recovery and trust-anchor governance remain separate prerequisites. Credential possession is not proof of independent sensing or absence of Sybil producers.

result.observation: The three mechanisms form an authenticity ladder, not interchangeable identifiers: nonce/UUID provides uniqueness only; immutable repository-object identity provides replay-stable object/event identity within the repository trust domain; signed/authenticated provenance can prove credential possession over a canonical tuple but inherits key/trust governance.
result.inference: For the exact p1-sa-600 evidence-handoff model, CanonicalInstanceID should state the narrow event/object identity actually replayed, while ProvenanceCommitment should separately encode any authentication claim. Do not label producer-chosen uniqueness as authenticity, and do not treat a repository object ID as producer identity. Signed provenance may strengthen the package only when the verifier has an independently defined trust rule for the credential; otherwise the authenticity child remains unresolved.
result.package_completeness: pass for preserving the distinction between byte uniqueness, repository-object identity and credential-bound provenance; fail as a complete arbitrary-producer authenticity solution because no zero-trust key/producer binding was established
result.replayability: pass for deterministic replay of the encoded identity/authentication claims given the same canonical fields; semantic authenticity remains conditional on repository and credential trust rules
result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact symbolic slice: local deterministic reasoning plus lightweight repository state/evidence transport only
result.quota_zero_assessment: The representation and verification-rule separation itself needs no hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute/storage, paid API/model, artifact service or finite credit. Any future mechanism that requires manual key ceremony, paid signing infrastructure, protected execution or finite hosted quota remains unresolved and cannot count as acceptance evidence.
result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: semantically consumed only frozen sanitized controls and own scientist_agents LATEST/p1-sa-600. No O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, protected-primary, manual-user, scheduler or public-source semantics were used.
